title: The Power of Habit, lesson 1 - your life runs on autopilot

slides.title: Why You Do Things You Never _Decided_ To Do
You're Not Choosing As Much As You Think
body: You wake up. Check your phone. Brush your teeth. Drive the same route.
It feels like you're in charge.
But most of it happens **before you decide anything.**
One man's strange story shows why.

slides.title: Meet The Man Who Couldn't Remember
body: **Eugene Pauly** lived in California with his wife, Beverly.
In 1992, a viral infection destroyed the parts of his brain that **store new memories.**
Afterwards, he couldn't hold onto a new fact for more than *a few moments.*

slides.title: He Couldn't Draw His Own House
body: After his illness, Eugene and Beverly moved into a **new house.**
When scientists asked him to sketch its layout, he couldn't.
Yet when he felt hungry, he'd walk *straight to the kitchen* and find a snack.

slides.title: He Never Got Lost On His Walk
body: Eugene took a walk around his neighbourhood **every day.**
Beverly feared he'd get lost. He couldn't even describe where he lived.
But each time, he found his way home, _with no idea how._

slides.title: Then A Scientist Put It To The Test
body: Memory researcher **Larry Squire** showed Eugene pairs of objects. One of each pair was marked as correct underneath.
Over weeks, Eugene picked the right ones **more and more often**...
...with *no memory* of ever seeing them.

slides.title: Habits Live In A Different Part Of Your Brain
body: Squire concluded that habits live in an older brain region, the _basal ganglia_, which Eugene's illness had spared.
Memory and habit run on **separate tracks.**
So a habit can keep working *even when you don't know why* you're doing it.

slides.title: And It's Not Just Eugene

graphic.label: of daily actions are habits, not decisions
graphic.caption: 2006 Duke University study, cited by Duhigg

body: Duhigg cites a 2006 Duke University study suggesting **more than 40%** of our daily actions are habits, not decisions.
That's almost _half your day_ on autopilot.

slides.title: You're Doing Them, Not Choosing Them
body: Think about:
You're doing them. But you're **not really choosing them.**

slides.title: The Good News: Autopilot Can Be Steered
body: This is unsettling. But it's also **good news.**
If so much of life runs on autopilot, then *noticing* the pattern is the first step to changing it.
You can't steer what you can't see.

slides.title: Try The One-Hour Watch
body: Tomorrow, pick one ordinary hour and **watch yourself closely.**

body.big: How many things happen before you decide to do them?

slides.title: Save This For Tomorrow Morning
body: Most of your day isn't decided. **It's repeated.**
Notice the pattern, then steer it.
